# Learnings and mistakes

No structural facts are generated for this page; the store has no concept of a mistake, only of records, decisions and handovers. Everything here is written by hand.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
1. A fix at one call site of a shared shape, while a sibling keeps the shape, is not a
   fix. The reviewer named cmd_zip because that is where it looked. cmd_skeleton carried
   the identical unguarded copy and was WORSE: unfixed it did not raise at all, it
   silently overwrote an external file and returned exit 0 reporting success. Enumerate
   the file, do not patch the line.
2. Reviewing a write site by READING it is not review. I wrote the inventory sentence
   clearing the new copy, in the same session that then shipped the defect, and the
   sentence was false the moment the destination was a symlink. Reasoning about it
   produced a confident wrong answer; running it would not have.
3. A cross-family gate is not ceremony. Local evidence at the moment of the miss: three
   suites green, five full gates ALL GREEN, the write-site inventory satisfied, five
   registry claims clean and non-overlapping. All true, none sufficient, because tests
   written by one family share that family's blind spots.
4. Reproduce before believing, in BOTH directions. Nothing here was accepted on sight,
   because this estate has a recorded case of a vivid review reaching the founder inside
   an hour that six later attempts could not reproduce. This time it reproduced eight of
   eight. The discipline is what makes either answer trustworthy.
5. My own mistakes, named rather than smoothed: I rewrote all 61 lines of a manifest to
   change one number, and had to revert and redo it as two lines. I wrote an evidence
   file outside my declared fence and the scope hook caught me. I dispatched an agent
   whose only deliverable was a path I had claimed in neither registry. I reflexively
   put rm -rf into a command and the permission gate refused it, correctly.
<!-- bm-human:end -->
